projects.title: The Smart Blinker
projects.wiring:
1. Insert LED into breadboard (long leg positive, short leg negative)
2. Connect 220-ohm resistor to LED's negative leg
3. Connect resistor's other end to Arduino GND
4. Connect LED's positive leg to Arduino Pin 13
5. Ensure proper polarity - LED won't work if reversed
steps: Step 1: Identify LED legs (long = positive/Anode, short = negative/Cathode)
Step 2: Place LED on breadboard across center gap
Step 3: Connect 220Ω resistor from LED negative leg to breadboard negative rail
Step 4: Connect breadboard negative rail to Arduino GND pin
Step 5: Connect LED positive leg to Arduino Digital Pin 13
Step 6: Upload the code and watch LED blink every second!
projects.logic: Basic digital output control - sending electricity to an output device. This is the fundamental concept of robotics: controlling hardware with code.
projects.description: The 'Hello World' of robotics. Learn how to send electricity to an output device.

projects.title: Digital Doorbell
projects.wiring:
1. Connect button across breadboard center gap
2. Connect 10k resistor from button to GND (pull-down)
3. Connect button to Arduino Pin 2
4. Connect buzzer positive to Pin 8, negative to GND
5. Button other side to 5V pin
steps: Step 1: Place push button on breadboard (straddles center gap)
Step 2: Connect 10kΩ resistor from one button pin to GND rail
Step 3: Connect same button pin to Arduino Digital Pin 2
Step 4: Connect opposite button pin to 5V pin on Arduino
Step 5: Connect buzzer positive (+) to Arduino Pin 8
Step 6: Connect buzzer negative (-) to GND rail
Step 7: Upload code, press button to hear sound!
projects.logic: Digital input triggering output - learn how physical buttons interact with microcontrollers to create sound feedback systems.
projects.description: Learn how to use a digital input (button) to trigger a sound output.

projects.title: Automatic Night Light
projects.wiring:
1. Create LDR voltage divider with 10k resistor
2. Connect LDR-resistor junction to Analog Pin A0
3. Connect LED with resistor to Pin 9
4. LDR to 5V, resistor to GND
5. LED negative to GND
steps: Step 1: Place LDR on breadboard (2 legs in different rows)
Step 2: Connect 10kΩ resistor in series with LDR
Step 3: Connect junction between LDR and resistor to Arduino A0
Step 4: Connect LDR other end to 5V, resistor other end to GND
Step 5: Connect LED with 220Ω resistor to Pin 9
Step 6: Cover LDR with hand - LED should turn on automatically!
Step 7: Open Serial Monitor to see light values (Tools → Serial Monitor)
projects.logic: Analog sensing and conditional control - robots 'feel' their environment using sensors and react autonomously.
projects.description: Learn how robots 'feel' the environment using analog sensors.

projects.title: Distance Radar
projects.wiring:
1. VCC (Ultrasonic) to 5V Arduino
2. GND to GND Arduino
3. Trig to Pin 11
4. Echo to Pin 12
5. Place sensor facing forward
steps: Step 1: Place HC-SR04 sensor on breadboard (4 pins)
Step 2: Connect VCC pin (usually leftmost) to Arduino 5V
Step 3: Connect GND pin to Arduino GND
Step 4: Connect TRIG pin to Arduino Digital Pin 11
Step 5: Connect ECHO pin to Arduino Digital Pin 12
Step 6: Open Serial Monitor (9600 baud)
Step 7: Place object in front - see distance measurements!
Step 8: Experiment with different materials (closer/farther)
projects.logic: Ultrasonic time-of-flight measurement - essential for self-driving cars, robotics navigation, and proximity detection systems.
projects.description: Use sound waves to measure distance, just like a self-driving car.

projects.title: Servo Sweep
projects.wiring:
1. Orange/Yellow (Signal) to Pin 9
2. Red (VCC) to 5V Arduino
3. Brown/Black (GND) to GND Arduino
4. Connect external power if using multiple servos
steps: Step 1: Identify servo wires: Orange/Yellow = Signal, Red = Power, Brown/Black = Ground
Step 2: Connect signal wire (orange) to Arduino Digital Pin 9
Step 3: Connect power wire (red) to Arduino 5V pin
Step 4: Connect ground wire (brown) to Arduino GND pin
Step 5: Upload the sweep code
Step 6: Watch servo move 0° → 90° → 180° continuously
Step 7: Modify delay values to change speed
Step 8: Try different angles (0, 45, 90, 135, 180)
projects.logic: Precise angular position control - servos are used in robotics arms, camera pan-tilt systems, and automated mechanisms.
projects.description: Control a motor that moves to specific angles (0° to 180°).

projects.title: Traffic Light System
projects.wiring:
1. Red LED: Pin 10 with resistor to GND
2. Yellow LED: Pin 11 with resistor to GND
3. Green LED: Pin 12 with resistor to GND
4. All cathodes (short legs) to GND rail
5. Use breadboard power rails for organization
steps: Step 1: Place three LEDs in a row: Red, Yellow, Green
Step 2: Connect 220Ω resistor to each LED's negative leg
Step 3: Connect all resistor ends to GND rail
Step 4: Connect Red LED positive to Arduino Pin 10
Step 5: Connect Yellow LED positive to Arduino Pin 11
Step 6: Connect Green LED positive to Arduino Pin 12
Step 7: Upload traffic light sequence code
Step 8: Observe sequence: Green(5s) → Yellow(2s) → Red(5s)
Step 9: Modify timing for different traffic patterns
projects.logic: Sequential timing and state management - essential for automation systems, industrial controls, and process sequencing.
projects.description: Learn how to manage multiple outputs using precise timing sequences.

projects.title: LCD Message Board
projects.wiring:
1. GND to GND Arduino
2. VCC to 5V Arduino
3. SDA to Pin A4 (or SDA pin)
4. SCL to Pin A5 (or SCL pin)
5. Adjust I2C address if needed (usually 0x27 or 0x3F)
steps: Step 1: Identify I2C LCD pins: GND, VCC, SDA, SCL
Step 2: Connect GND to Arduino GND
Step 3: Connect VCC to Arduino 5V
Step 4: Connect SDA to Arduino A4 (or SDA pin)
Step 5: Connect SCL to Arduino A5 (or SCL pin)
Step 6: Upload LCD test code
Step 7: If no display, adjust contrast potentiometer on I2C module
Step 8: Change message in code to display your text
Step 9: Try scrolling text or displaying sensor values
projects.logic: I2C communication and text display - learn serial communication protocols and human-machine interfaces.
projects.description: Moving beyond blinking lights to displaying actual text and data.

projects.title: Security Lock
projects.wiring:
1. Keypad rows: Pins 2,3,4,5
2. Keypad columns: Pins 6,7,8,9
3. Servo signal to Pin 10
4. Servo power to 5V, GND to GND
5. Use external power for servo if needed
steps: Step 1: Connect keypad ROW pins to Arduino Pins 2,3,4,5
Step 2: Connect keypad COLUMN pins to Arduino Pins 6,7,8,9
Step 3: Connect servo signal (orange) to Pin 10
Step 4: Connect servo power (red) to 5V
Step 5: Connect servo ground (brown) to GND
Step 6: Upload security lock code
Step 7: Default password is '1234'
Step 8: Enter correct password - servo opens gate for 3 seconds
Step 9: Try wrong password - nothing happens
Step 10: Change password in code for customization
projects.logic: Matrix input processing and password validation - learn secure access control systems and input matrix scanning.
projects.description: Learn how to process matrix inputs for password-protected devices.

projects.title: Smart Plant Watering
projects.wiring:
1. Soil sensor: Signal to A0, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
2. Relay: Signal to Pin 7, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
3. Pump: Positive to relay NO, Negative to power supply GND
4. External 5V supply for pump
5. Use relay to control pump power
steps: Step 1: Connect soil moisture sensor: A0 to Arduino A0, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 2: Connect relay module: IN to Pin 7, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 3: Connect water pump to relay: Positive to NO terminal, Negative to power supply
Step 4: Connect external 5V power supply for pump
Step 5: Place soil sensor in plant pot
Step 6: Upload code and test with dry soil
Step 7: Pump runs for 2 seconds when soil is dry
Step 8: Adjust moisture threshold (500 in code)
Step 9: Place pump in water container, tube to plant
Warning: Keep electronics away from water!
projects.logic: Action-reaction automation - sensors trigger actuators to create intelligent systems that maintain optimal conditions.
projects.description: Introduction to 'Action-Reaction' automation for plant care.

projects.title: IR Remote Control
projects.wiring:
1. IR receiver: OUT to Pin 11, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
2. LED with resistor to Pin 13
3. Ensure IR receiver faces remote
4. Use TV/DVD remote for testing
5. Check IR library compatibility
steps: Step 1: Identify IR receiver pins: GND, VCC, OUT (check datasheet)
Step 2: Connect OUT to Arduino Pin 11
Step 3: Connect VCC to Arduino 5V
Step 4: Connect GND to Arduino GND
Step 5: Connect LED with 220Ω resistor to Pin 13
Step 6: Install IRremote library (Sketch → Include Library → Manage Libraries)
Step 7: Upload IR receiver code
Step 8: Point any remote at sensor and press buttons
Step 9: LED toggles with each button press
Step 10: Open Serial Monitor to see button codes
projects.logic: Infrared signal decoding - learn wireless communication protocols and remote control systems used in home automation.
projects.description: Understanding wireless communication using infrared signals.

projects.title: Obstacle Avoiding Robot
projects.wiring:
1. Motors to L298N: OUT1-OUT4
2. L298N inputs: IN1-IN4 to Pins 5,6,10,11
3. Ultrasonic: Trig(11), Echo(12)
4. Servo on Pin 9
5. External battery for motors
6. Arduino power from battery or USB
steps: Step 1: Assemble 2WD chassis with motors and wheels
Step 2: Connect motors to L298N: Motor A to OUT1-OUT2, Motor B to OUT3-OUT4
Step 3: Connect L298N inputs: IN1 to Pin 5, IN2 to Pin 6, IN3 to Pin 10, IN4 to Pin 11
Step 4: Connect L298N power: 12V to battery positive, GND to battery negative
Step 5: Connect L298N 5V to Arduino 5V (for logic)
Step 6: Connect ultrasonic sensor: Trig to Pin 11, Echo to Pin 12
Step 7: Connect servo to Pin 9
Step 8: Mount sensors on chassis
Step 9: Upload obstacle avoidance code
Step 10: Test robot in open space with obstacles
Step 11: Adjust distance threshold (20cm in code) as needed
projects.logic: Autonomous decision making with sensor fusion - create robots that navigate environments intelligently using multiple sensors.
projects.description: Build a 'Self-Thinking' car that navigates a room without hitting walls.

projects.title: Line Follower Robot
projects.wiring:
1. Left IR Sensor to Digital Pin A0
2. Right IR Sensor to Digital Pin A1
3. Motors to L298N driver
4. L298N inputs to Pins 5,6,10,11
steps: Step 1: Mount IR sensors at front of chassis (2-3cm above ground)
Step 2: Connect left sensor OUT to A0, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 3: Connect right sensor OUT to A1, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 4: Calibrate sensors: White surface = LOW, Black line = HIGH
Step 5: Connect motors to L298N driver
Step 6: Connect L298N to Arduino Pins 5,6,10,11
Step 7: Create black line track on white surface
Step 8: Upload line follower code
Step 9: Test robot on track - adjust sensor height if needed
Step 10: Experiment with different line patterns
projects.logic: Infrared line detection and differential steering - industrial automation, warehouse robots, and manufacturing line systems.
projects.description: Use infrared sensors to make the robot follow a specific track on the floor.

projects.title: Weather Station
projects.wiring:
1. DHT11 Data to Pin 2
2. LCD SDA to A4, SCL to A5
3. VCC to 5V, GND to GND for both
steps: Step 1: Connect DHT11: Data to Pin 2, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 2: Connect LCD I2C: SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 3: Install DHT library (Adafruit DHT library)
Step 4: Upload weather station code
Step 5: LCD displays temperature (°C) and humidity (%)
Step 6: Breathe on sensor to see humidity change
Step 7: Place near heat source to see temperature change
Step 8: Add more sensors (pressure, rain) for advanced version
projects.logic: Sensor data acquisition and display - learn environmental monitoring and data presentation for smart agriculture and home automation.
projects.description: Learn to read data from environmental sensors and display it on LCD.

projects.title: RFID Smart Gate
projects.wiring:
1. RFID: SDA(10), SCK(13), MOSI(11), MISO(12), RST(9)
2. Servo to Pin 3
3. Buzzer to Pin 8
steps: Step 1: Connect RFID module: SDA to Pin 10, SCK to 13, MOSI to 11, MISO to 12, RST to 9
Step 2: Connect servo to Pin 3
Step 3: Connect buzzer to Pin 8
Step 4: Install MFRC522 library
Step 5: Upload RFID gate code
Step 6: Scan your RFID card/tag
Step 7: Note the UID in Serial Monitor
Step 8: Replace UID in code with your card's UID
Step 9: Scan authorized card - servo opens gate
Step 10: Scan unauthorized card - buzzer sounds
projects.logic: RFID authentication and access control - security systems, attendance tracking, and smart office applications.
projects.description: Create a security system where only specific RFID cards can open a gate.

projects.title: Bluetooth Controlled Car
projects.wiring:
1. HC-05 TX to Arduino RX (Pin 0)
2. HC-05 RX to Arduino TX (Pin 1)
3. Motors to L298N
4. L298N to Pins 5,6,10,11
steps: Step 1: Disconnect Arduino from USB before connecting HC-05
Step 2: Connect HC-05: TX to RX (Pin 0), RX to TX (Pin 1), VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 3: Connect motors to L298N driver
Step 4: Connect L298N to Arduino Pins 5,6,10,11
Step 5: Download Bluetooth RC Car app on smartphone
Step 6: Upload Bluetooth car code
Step 7: Pair HC-05 with phone (default PIN: 1234 or 0000)
Step 8: Use app to control robot: F(Forward), B(Back), L(Left), R(Right), S(Stop)
Step 9: Test control range (typically 10 meters)
Step 10: Add obstacle avoidance for autonomous mode
projects.logic: Bluetooth serial communication and motor control - wireless robot control, smartphone integration, and IoT applications.
projects.description: Control your robot wirelessly using a smartphone app via Bluetooth.

projects.title: Gas Leakage Alarm
projects.wiring:
1. MQ-2: A0 to Arduino A0, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
2. Buzzer positive to Pin 8, negative to GND
3. Red LED with 220Ω resistor to Pin 7
4. Optional: Add green LED to Pin 6 for normal indication
steps: Step 1: Connect MQ-2 sensor: A0 to Arduino A0, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 2: Connect buzzer: Positive (+) to Pin 8, Negative (-) to GND
Step 3: Connect red LED with 220Ω resistor to Pin 7 (alarm indicator)
Step 4: Optional: Connect green LED with resistor to Pin 6 (safe indicator)
Step 5: Upload gas detection code
Step 6: Open Serial Monitor to see gas values (normal: 100-300)
Step 7: Test with lighter gas (butane) - DO NOT light it!
Step 8: When gas > 400, buzzer sounds and red LED lights
Step 9: Adjust threshold value in code for sensitivity
Step 10: Place in kitchen for LPG leak detection
projects.logic: Gas concentration monitoring and alarm triggering - industrial safety systems, home safety devices, and environmental monitoring.
projects.description: A safety robot that detects smoke or gas leaks and sounds a loud alarm.

projects.title: Touchless Dustbin
projects.wiring:
1. Ultrasonic: Trig to Pin 2, Echo to Pin 3, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
2. Servo: Signal to Pin 9, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
3. Mount servo on dustbin lid
4. Ensure sensor faces outward
steps: Step 1: Connect ultrasonic sensor: Trig to Pin 2, Echo to Pin 3, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 2: Connect servo: Signal (orange) to Pin 9, VCC (red) to 5V, GND (brown) to GND
Step 3: Take a small dustbin or make one from cardboard
Step 4: Attach servo to dustbin lid using glue or tape
Step 5: Mount ultrasonic sensor on front of dustbin
Step 6: Ensure servo can open/close lid fully (0° to 90°)
Step 7: Upload touchless dustbin code
Step 8: Test by waving hand 10-15cm from sensor
Step 9: Lid should open for 3 seconds then close
Step 10: Adjust detection distance in code (15cm)
projects.logic: Proximity detection and automated response - hygiene-focused automation, public health applications, and touchless interfaces.
projects.description: A hygiene-focused project where the bin lid opens automatically when you wave your hand.

projects.title: Gesture Controlled Robot
projects.wiring:
TRANSMITTER (Hand Module):
1. MPU6050: SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
2. HC-05: TX to RX (Pin 0), RX to TX (Pin 1), VCC to 5V, GND to GND

RECEIVER (Robot):
1. HC-05: TX to RX (Pin 0), RX to TX (Pin 1)
2. L298N: IN1-IN4 to Pins 5,6,10,11
3. Motors to L298N outputs
steps: Step 1: BUILD TRANSMITTER (Hand Module):
• Connect MPU6050: SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
• Connect HC-05: TX to RX (Pin 0), RX to TX (Pin 1), VCC to 5V, GND to GND
• Upload transmitter code to first Arduino
• Mount on glove or wrist band
Step 2: BUILD RECEIVER (Robot):
• Assemble 2WD robot chassis
• Connect motors to L298N driver
• Connect L298N to Arduino: IN1-4 to Pins 5,6,10,11
• Connect second HC-05: TX to RX, RX to TX
• Upload receiver code to second Arduino
Step 3: PAIRING:
• Pair both HC-05 modules (default PIN: 1234)
• One module must be in MASTER mode (AT+ROLE=1)
• Other in SLAVE mode (AT+ROLE=0)
Step 4: TESTING:
• Power both circuits
• Tilt hand forward → Robot moves forward
• Tilt hand backward → Robot moves backward
• Tilt left → Robot turns left
• Tilt right → Robot turns right
• Keep level → Robot stops
projects.logic: IMU data processing and wireless command transmission - gesture recognition, human-robot interaction, and motion-based control systems.
projects.description: Control a robot by simply tilting your hand using accelerometer data.

projects.title: Rain Sensing Roof
projects.wiring:
1. Rain Sensor: AO to A1, DO not connected, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
2. Servo: Signal to Pin 10, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
3. Buzzer: Positive to Pin 8, Negative to GND
4. Build miniature roof structure
steps: Step 1: Build miniature roof using cardboard or popsicle sticks
Step 2: Attach servo to roof mechanism so it can open/close
Step 3: Connect rain sensor: AO to A1, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 4: Connect servo: Signal to Pin 10, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 5: Connect buzzer to Pin 8 (rain alert)
Step 6: Upload rain sensing code
Step 7: Test with few drops of water on sensor
Step 8: Sensor value should drop (dry: ~1023, wet: <700)
Step 9: When wet, roof closes and buzzer beeps
Step 10: Roof opens when sensor dries
Step 11: Place project near window for real rain detection
projects.logic: Rain detection and automated shelter mechanism - smart agriculture, weather-responsive systems, and automated protection devices.
projects.description: A smart home project where a roof closes automatically when it starts raining.

projects.title: IoT Weather Station
projects.wiring:
1. DHT11: Data to D2 (GPIO4), VCC to 3.3V, GND to GND
2. No external power needed - USB powered
3. Ensure stable WiFi connection
4. Create Thingspeak account for cloud data
steps: Step 1: Set up Thingspeak account (free at thingspeak.com)
Step 2: Create new channel, note Channel ID and Write API Key
Step 3: Connect DHT11 to NodeMCU: Data to D2, VCC to 3.3V, GND to GND
Step 4: Install required libraries:
• DHT sensor library
• Adafruit Unified Sensor
• ESP8266WiFi
Step 5: Modify code with your:
• WiFi SSID and Password
• Thingspeak API Key
• Channel ID
Step 6: Upload code to NodeMCU
Step 7: Open Serial Monitor (115200 baud)
Step 8: Wait for WiFi connection confirmation
Step 9: Check Thingspeak channel for incoming data
Step 10: View temperature/humidity graphs online
Step 11: Add more sensors (pressure, light) to same channel
projects.logic: WiFi connectivity and cloud data transmission - IoT systems, remote monitoring, and cloud-based data analytics.
projects.description: Send temperature and humidity data to the cloud using IoT technology.

projects.title: Smart Parking System
projects.wiring:
ULTRASONIC SENSORS:
1. Sensor 1: Trig(2), Echo(3), VCC(5V), GND(GND)
2. Sensor 2: Trig(4), Echo(5), VCC(5V), GND(GND)
3. Sensor 3: Trig(6), Echo(7), VCC(5V), GND(GND)

LED INDICATORS:
1. Red LED: Pin 8 (Slot 1 occupied)
2. Green LED: Pin 9 (Slot 1 empty)
3. Yellow LED: Pin 10 (Slot 2/3 indicator)

LCD DISPLAY:
1. SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
steps: Step 1: SET UP PARKING SLOTS:
• Create 3 parking spaces using cardboard
• Mount ultrasonic sensors above each slot
• Sensors should point downward to detect cars
Step 2: CONNECT ULTRASONIC SENSORS:
• Slot 1: Trig(2), Echo(3)
• Slot 2: Trig(4), Echo(5)
• Slot 3: Trig(6), Echo(7)
• All VCC to 5V, all GND to common GND
Step 3: CONNECT LED INDICATORS:
• Red LED (Slot 1 occupied): Pin 8 with 220Ω resistor
• Green LED (Slot 1 empty): Pin 9 with resistor
• Yellow LED (General): Pin 10 with resistor
Step 4: CONNECT LCD:
• SDA to A4, SCL to A5
• VCC to 5V, GND to GND
• Adjust contrast if needed
Step 5: UPLOAD CODE:
• Upload smart parking system code
• Open Serial Monitor for debugging
Step 6: TESTING:
• Place object in Slot 1 → Red LED lights
• Empty Slot 1 → Green LED lights
• LCD shows available slots count
• Try different combinations of occupied slots
Step 7: ENHANCEMENTS:
• Add buzzer for full parking
• Add more slots with multiplexing
• Create entry/exit gates
projects.logic: Multi-sensor monitoring and availability display - smart city infrastructure, resource management, and real-time monitoring systems.
projects.description: Build a smart parking system that shows available parking slots.

projects.title: Voice Controlled Robot
projects.wiring:
1. HC-05: TX to RX (Pin 0), RX to TX (Pin 1), VCC to 5V, GND to GND
2. L298N: IN1-IN4 to Pins 5,6,10,11
3. Motors to L298N outputs
4. External battery for motors
5. Arduino powered via USB or battery
steps: Step 1: BUILD ROBOT BASE:
• Assemble 2WD chassis with motors
• Connect motors to L298N driver
• Connect L298N to Arduino Pins 5,6,10,11
• Connect power supply for motors
Step 2: CONNECT BLUETOOTH:
• Connect HC-05: TX to RX (Pin 0), RX to TX (Pin 1)
• Connect VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 3: INSTALL VOICE APP:
• Download 'Arduino Voice Control' or 'BT Voice Control' app
• Or use 'Google Assistant' with IFTTT
Step 4: UPLOAD CODE:
• Upload voice control code to Arduino
• Open Serial Monitor to see incoming commands
Step 5: PAIR AND TEST:
• Pair HC-05 with smartphone (PIN: 1234)
• Open voice control app
• Train voice commands:
- 'Forward' or 'Go' → Robot moves forward
- 'Backward' or 'Back' → Robot moves backward
- 'Left' → Robot turns left
- 'Right' → Robot turns right
- 'Stop' or 'Halt' → Robot stops
Step 6: TROUBLESHOOTING:
• Check Serial Monitor for received commands
• Ensure proper voice recognition training
• Adjust motor speed in code if needed
Step 7: ENHANCEMENTS:
• Add obstacle avoidance while voice controlled
• Add voice feedback (speaker module)
• Implement gesture + voice hybrid control
projects.logic: Voice command processing via Bluetooth - natural language processing, voice interfaces, and accessibility technologies.
projects.description: Control your robot using voice commands through a smartphone app.

projects.title: Smart Street Light
projects.wiring:
1. LDR: One leg to 5V, other leg to A0 with 10k resistor to GND
2. PIR Sensor: OUT to Pin 2, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
3. Relay: IN to Pin 8, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
4. LED Strip: Positive to relay COM, Negative to power GND
5. External 12V for LED strip
steps: Step 1: UNDERSTAND THE LOGIC:
• Light turns ON when: 1) It's dark AND 2) Motion detected
• Light stays ON for 30 seconds after last motion
• During daytime, light stays OFF regardless of motion
Step 2: CONNECT LDR (Light Sensor):
• Create voltage divider: LDR between 5V and A0
• 10k resistor between A0 and GND
• Cover LDR to simulate darkness
Step 3: CONNECT PIR (Motion Sensor):
• OUT to Pin 2
• VCC to 5V, GND to GND
• Adjust sensitivity and time delay pots on PIR
Step 4: CONNECT RELAY:
• IN to Pin 8
• VCC to 5V, GND to GND
• Connect LED strip to relay COM and NO terminals
Step 5: POWER CONNECTION:
• Connect 12V power supply to LED strip via relay
• Arduino powered via USB
• NEVER connect high voltage directly to Arduino!
Step 6: UPLOAD CODE:
• Upload smart street light code
• Open Serial Monitor to see sensor values
Step 7: TESTING:
• Cover LDR (simulate night)
• Wave hand in front of PIR
• Light should turn ON for 30 seconds
• Uncover LDR (daytime) → Light stays OFF
Step 8: CALIBRATION:
• Adjust LDR threshold in code (500)
• Adjust PIR sensitivity screw
• Change ON duration (30000ms = 30 seconds)
projects.logic: Dual-sensor optimization for energy efficiency - smart city applications, energy conservation, and adaptive lighting systems.
projects.description: Build an energy-efficient street light that turns on only when dark and motion is detected.

projects.title: Home Automation System
projects.wiring:
BLUETOOTH CONNECTION:
1. HC-05: TX to RX (Pin 0), RX to TX (Pin 1), VCC to 5V, GND to GND

RELAY MODULE:
1. IN1 to Pin 5 (Relay 1)
2. IN2 to Pin 6 (Relay 2)
3. IN3 to Pin 7 (Relay 3)
4. IN4 to Pin 8 (Relay 4)
5. VCC to 5V, GND to GND

APPLIANCES:
1. Connect bulbs to relay COM and NO terminals
2. Use separate 220V power supply for appliances
3. CAUTION: High voltage! Ask teacher/parent for help
steps: Step 1: SAFETY FIRST:
• This project involves HIGH VOLTAGE (220V)
• Work with teacher/parent supervision
• Keep all high voltage connections insulated
• Turn OFF main power when making connections
Step 2: CONNECT BLUETOOTH:
• HC-05: TX to RX (Pin 0), RX to TX (Pin 1)
• VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Step 3: CONNECT RELAY MODULE:
• IN1 to Pin 5, IN2 to Pin 6, IN3 to Pin 7, IN4 to Pin 8
• VCC to 5V, GND to GND
• Ensure relay module is 5V compatible
Step 4: HIGH VOLTAGE CONNECTIONS (WITH SUPERVISION):
• Connect 4 bulbs to relay outputs
• Relay COM → Live wire from mains
• Relay NO → Bulb live wire
• Bulb neutral → Direct to mains neutral
• Double-check all connections before powering
Step 5: INSTALL BLUETOOTH APP:
• Download 'Bluetooth Terminal' or 'Arduino Bluetooth Control'
• Or create custom app with MIT App Inventor
Step 6: UPLOAD CODE:
• Upload home automation code
• Open Serial Monitor to test commands
Step 7: TESTING (LOW VOLTAGE FIRST):
• Connect LEDs instead of bulbs for initial testing
• Send commands via Serial Monitor:
- 'relay1' → Toggle relay 1
- 'relay2' → Toggle relay 2
- 'all on' → Turn all relays ON
- 'all off' → Turn all relays OFF
Step 8: FINAL TEST (WITH SUPERVISION):
• Replace LEDs with actual bulbs
• Control home appliances via smartphone
• Create automation schedules in code

projects.title: Automatic Sanitizer Dispenser
projects.wiring:
1. Ultrasonic Sensor: Trig(2), Echo(3), VCC(5V), GND(GND)
2. Servo Motor: Signal(9), VCC(5V), GND(GND)
3. Mount servo to press sanitizer pump
4. Position sensor to detect hand
5. Use cardboard for mounting structure
steps: Step 1: PREPARE SANITIZER BOTTLE:
• Use a pump-action sanitizer bottle
• Remove pump mechanism if possible
• Test that pressing pump dispenses sanitizer
Step 2: BUILD MOUNTING STRUCTURE:
• Create stand using cardboard or wood
• Mount servo motor so it can press pump
• Attach ultrasonic sensor facing outward
• Ensure hand can be placed 5-10cm from sensor
Step 3: CONNECT ULTRASONIC SENSOR:
• Trig to Pin 2, Echo to Pin 3
• VCC to 5V, GND to GND
• Position sensor to detect approaching hand
Step 4: CONNECT SERVO:
• Signal (orange) to Pin 9
• VCC (red) to 5V, GND (brown) to GND
• Attach servo arm to sanitizer pump
Step 5: CALIBRATE SERVO POSITIONS:
• 0° = Rest position (not pressing)
• 90° = Press position (dispensing)
• Test manually with servo sweep code first
Step 6: UPLOAD SANITIZER CODE:
• Upload automatic sanitizer code
• Open Serial Monitor to see distance readings
Step 7: TESTING:
• Place hand 5-10cm from sensor
• Servo should press pump for 0.5 seconds
• Wait 3 seconds before next detection
• Adjust detection distance in code (10cm)
Step 8: FINAL ASSEMBLY:
• Secure all components
• Add battery pack for portability
• Place near entrance for hygiene station
Step 9: ENHANCEMENTS:
• Add LED indicator when dispensing
• Add counter to track usage
• Add low sanitizer warning
